question: Is the new hold route (POST /displays/{screen_id}/show) bound to the admitted owner — the door's authority, his own conversation and a record that conversation was issued — before any tool runs, any record is read or any screen changes, given that put_held calls dispatch without passing the request?
answer: Yes. The chain, at this commit. The door: app/main.py guard_and_freshness refuses a request proxy_state calls forged, a proxied one with no login and a login not on the allow-list, then for every path that is not public asks principal_verdict (app/routes/actions.py: his login on the list and, with CROOKS_TAILSCALE_VERIFY on — production's unset value resolves to on, config/settings.py — Tailscale confirming the device is his; a request made on the server itself only when CROOKS_WRITES_LOCAL_OWNER or CROOKS_LOCAL_OWNER says so, and both are off in production) and answers 403 before any route runs. The screens router asks the same rule again as its own dependency (displays.router: Depends(require_principal)). The route: show_held -> put.put_held -> put._put, which refuses, in this order and before anything is dispatched or read: a kind a screen does not show (422; HeldBody takes session_id, kind and ref and nothing else); a conversation CLIVE has let go of (409 no_session) or one bound to another login (403 wrong_session, session_matches); a screen that is gone (404 not_found) or waiting for its code (409 not_approved); and a record THAT conversation was not issued — classify(SHOW_TOOL, args, session.issued_ids) is DENY, because screen_show's issued-id arguments (order_id, objective_id) are optional in its schema, so an absent one is skipped and a supplied one must be in the session's issued ids (gate._check_issued_ids) — 403 not_issued. question: On the live provider, do Claude's tool calls keep the prepare-only boundary — does a write the model calls pass through the gate and stage a proposal, with no mutation executed before the owner's gesture?
answer: Yes. MaxAgentSDKProvider._options gives the Agent SDK no built-in tools (tools=[]), only CLIVE's in-process MCP server built from the registry, with the tools it withholds disallowed as well, permission_mode 'dontAsk', no settings inherited, and a PreToolUse hook (make_pretooluse_hook, app/tools/dispatch.py) that fires on every call and denies what the gate denies. The MCP server's handler for every tool is the provider's _dispatch: refused without the turn's active owner authority, refused once the owner has moved on, then dispatch() under that authority. dispatch classifies the call (app/tools/gate.py); a write classifies STAGE_FOR_OWNER and goes to _stage, which runs the tool's own prepare from a fresh read and hands the result to ActionEngine.stage — a PENDING proposal on the session, nothing sent. The only code that executes a write is ActionEngine.commit, and its only callers are POST /actions/{id}/commit (after the owner's gesture: for a red card, the arm, the hold and its token) and the batch route's; no path from the provider reaches it. The test runs the provider's own code, not a stand-in for it: tests/test_r11_turn.py `sdk` replaces only the `claude` subprocess (Cli), which runs the provider's own hook and its own in-process tool handler on a task carrying none of the request's context, as the SDK does; a refund, a cancellation and a store credit asked for out loud are each a red PENDING card, a commit without the hold is 409 not_armed, a spoken 'yes' applies nothing, the same change on a record the conversation never read is denied by the hook, and sdk.store.mutations == [] throughout.

question: Does the made-once write boundary stop a second order or credit being made from one card, for concurrent, unarmed and retried commits — is its reservation atomic, and is it correctly released afterwards?
answer: FIXED in round 13: 05564a5f, then a7c4e6d1 after the round-13 independent check; d65cf011 made every surface say what the card says. The reservation was atomic; its release was bound neither to the commit that made it nor to that commit's outcome. Atomic, then and now: in POST /actions/{id}/commit, workspaces.commit_refused, workspaces.before_commit and the engine's claim run with no await between them (app/routes/actions.py; app/actions/engine.py commit awaits nothing before `proposal.status = EXECUTING`), so of two hold cards of one card committed at once the second finds the card `sending` and is 409 already_made with nothing sent; a retry of the same card waits for the first commit's outcome and is handed it (_terminal: already_executed, never a second send); Prepare while it sends is refused; a commit without its hold is 409 not_armed and leaves the card his. The defect, at 361b0138: before_commit noted `sending, by=commit` with no proposal id, and after_commit removed that note for ANY proposal of the workspace whose outcome was not VERIFIED, EXECUTED, UNVERIFIED or FAILED. A commit of a hold card the same card had withdrawn (it passes commit_refused, which refuses PENDING cards only) came back `revoked` and freed the card while another hold was still at its precondition read: Prepare was taken, a second hold card staged and held, and a second credit sent. The fix, in app/families/_workspace.py: before_commit notes the reservation as `sending, by=commit, proposal=<the committing proposal's id>` (with what a failed card said before, to say again if nothing is sent); ws.sending carries that proposal onto the notes it makes as the change leaves; and after_commit takes proof that the thing was made (VERIFIED) from any commit, and anything else only from the commit the reservation names — any other commit of the card returns without touching it. The independent check found the same hole in the reserving card's own retry: a commit that finds its proposal still EXECUTING or EXECUTED — a retried request, an Android double-fire — waits WAIT_FOR_OUTCOME_S (25 s) for the first commit's outcome and, failing that, is answered `in_progress` (ActionEngine.commit); after_commit took that answer for the outcome, since it names the same proposal and so passes the holder check. With the change already left, it noted the card UNCONFIRMED, which note() never lets fall back, so when Shopify then refused the first commit the card stayed 'sent, not confirmed' (and the retry was answered as that); with the first commit still at its precondition read, it fell through to the release, and the card was free for a second Prepare, and so a second credit or order, while the first was on its way. Now after_commit returns at once for a proposal still EXECUTING or EXECUTED: only the commit sending the change settles the card, when Shopify answers (a7c4e6d1). What the owner is told follows the card (d65cf011): sent_not_confirmed(proposal) is true only for the hold card whose own commit left its card UNCONFIRMED (the note names that proposal), and for it the commit route answers status and code 'unverified' with SENT_NOT_CONFIRMED ('Sent to Shopify, not confirmed. Check it in Shopify Admin before asking again.') as the spoken line and session.last_outcome, present_action draws the outcome card 'Could not confirm' with those words where the engine's code, service_unavailable, titled it 'Not applied' (_OUTCOME_WORDS), and /actions/states reports it 'unverified' on every reconciliation. Invariant: only the commit that reserved a card, and only with its own outcome, releases or settles it; anyone else's commit settles it only with proof that it was made. test_a_retry_answered_in_progress_does_not_lock_a_card_shopify_then_refuses failed at 604c7f92 with the retry answered 'unverified' ('Sent to Shopify, not confirmed') instead of in_progress, and test_a_retry_answered_in_progress_does_not_free_a_card_still_at_its_first_read with Prepare taken while the first commit was still reading; both pass now. test_s2a_03_a_withdrawn_hold_card_committed_meanwhile_leaves_the_sending_card_finished failed at 361b0138 with 'AssertionError: 2 credits sent: Prepare was taken while the first was being applied; balance now £55.00' and passes now: the stray commit is `revoked`, Prepare is refused, one credit. test_a_timed_out_credit_is_sent_not_confirmed_on_every_surface failed before d65cf011 with the commit answered ('failed', 'service_unavailable') and passes now; its edges — a credit that never left still says 'Not applied', one read back as landed says applied, one landed and unreadable says unverified and never 'Nothing was' — pass before and after. The stray-commit edge passes before and after: the same stray commit with nothing in flight reserves and releases only for itself — nothing is noted, the live hold card still gives its one £20 — and on a card whose send was proven never to have left, a stray commit of that failed card leaves it given back with its reason. The one-proposal-per-request rule in ActionEngine.stage normally keeps two hold cards of one card from waiting at once; the concurrency test sets it aside so that the route's own check is what is tested. Round 12's follow-up ruled this finding a defect but the record does not print its reasoning (followup-collected.json is on the server only); the defect fixed here is the one this boundary had.
